---
title: "Data model"
---

::: {.lead}
How SysNDD stores a gene-disease association: the entity, its reviews and statuses, the
evidence categories, and the identifiers that link each record to standard databases. Read
this page to interpret what you see in the web app, in downloads and in API responses.
:::

::: {.callout-note .who-can title="Who this is for"}
Everyone. No database knowledge is needed. Field names in `code` are the names used in API
responses and Excel downloads.
:::

## The entity: one gene, one inheritance, one disease

The unit of curation in SysNDD is the **entity**. An entity states that disease-causing variants
in one gene cause one disease through one mode of inheritance.

| Part | Standard | Example (entity 856) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gene | HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee (HGNC) | *CHD8*, `HGNC:20153` |
| Mode of inheritance | Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) | Autosomal dominant inheritance (`HP:0000006`) |
| Disease | Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM), or Mondo Disease Ontology (MONDO) where OMIM has no entry | Intellectual developmental disorder with autism and macrocephaly, `OMIM:615032` |

Each entity also records whether its disease is a neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD). The web app
shows this as **NDD Yes** or **NDD No**; API responses use `ndd_phenotype_word`.

Because the entity is the unit, one gene can have several entities. A gene that causes a
dominant and a recessive disorder has two entities. A gene linked to an NDD and to a heart
disease has two entities, one of which is outside the NDD scope.

The three parts of an entity never change once it is created. When a disease name or identifier
must be corrected, a Curator creates a new entity and deactivates the old one (see
[Versions and history](#versions-and-history)).

## What is stored about an entity

An entity collects two kinds of record over time: **reviews** and **statuses**.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "The parts of an entity. The entity is fixed; reviews and statuses are added over time, and one of each is active."
%%| label: fig-data-model-entity
%%| fig-alt: "Diagram: gene (HGNC), mode of inheritance (HPO) and disease (OMIM or MONDO) combine into one entity. The entity has reviews (synopsis, phenotypes, variation, publications) and statuses (evidence category); one of each is active."
flowchart TB
  G["Gene<br/>HGNC"] --> E
  I["Mode of inheritance<br/>HPO"] --> E
  D["Disease<br/>OMIM or MONDO"] --> E
  E(["Entity<br/>fixed triple + NDD yes/no"])
  E --> R["Reviews<br/>one active, earlier ones kept"]
  E --> S["Statuses<br/>one active, earlier ones kept"]
  R --> SY["Clinical synopsis"]
  R --> PH["Phenotypes<br/>HPO terms + modifier"]
  R --> VA["Variation<br/>VariO terms"]
  R --> PU["Publications<br/>PMIDs"]
  S --> C["Evidence category"]
```

### Review

A **review** is the curated description of an entity. It holds:

- **Clinical synopsis**: a short free-text summary of the published evidence and the clinical
  picture. The entity page shows it as **Clinical Synopsis**.
- **Phenotypes**: HPO terms, each with a modifier (see [Phenotypes](#phenotypes)).
- **Variation**: Variation Ontology (VariO) terms describing the types and consequences of the variants
  (see [Variation](#variation)).
- **Publications**: PubMed IDs. The entity page lists GeneReviews chapters separately as
  **Gene Reviews**; all other papers appear under **Publications**.
- The date of the review and an optional comment.

### Status

A **status** records the evidence category of the entity, its date and an optional comment.

### Approval

Reviewers and Curators submit new reviews and statuses. A submission is not public. It becomes
public only after a Curator or Administrator approves it. The web app, the downloads, the API
and the MCP server show only approved records.

## Evidence categories

Every entity has exactly one active category.

| Category | In short |
| --- | --- |
| [Definitive]{.cat .cat-definitive} | Published, and either a clear-cut frequency or cumulative evidence |
| [Moderate]{.cat .cat-moderate} | Published, intellectual disability indicated; too good for Limited, not good enough for Definitive |
| [Limited]{.cat .cat-limited} | Published, intellectual disability indicated, but limited genetic and/or clinical evidence |
| [Refuted]{.cat .cat-refuted} | Newer evidence contradicts the association |
| [Not applicable]{.cat .cat-na} | Entity outside the neurodevelopmental disorder (NDD) scope, kept for gene context; a tag, not an evidence category |

The rules for assigning Definitive, Moderate, Limited and Refuted are in
[Curation criteria](05-curation-criteria.qmd). The table above repeats the summary from that
chapter; the rules there govern.

**Not applicable** marks entities whose disease lies outside the NDD scope, for example a
cardiac disorder caused by a gene that also causes an NDD. SysNDD keeps these entities so that
each gene's full disease spectrum is visible. Not applicable is not a lower tier below Limited.
The web app and the API write it as `not applicable`; the curation criteria abbreviate it `n.a.`.
The NDD Yes/No flag and the category are recorded separately; filter on the category when you
need to exclude Not applicable entities.

Earlier publications and data files may call the categories by number. The numbers map to the
names as follows: Definitive (Category 1), Moderate (Category 2), Limited (Category 3). In the
API, `category_id` uses 1 to 5 in the order of the table above.

## Versions and history

SysNDD never deletes curation data. Each change adds a record:

- **New evidence.** A Reviewer or Curator submits a new review or status. After approval it
  becomes the active one. Earlier reviews and statuses stay in the database.
- **Category change.** An entity is moved to a higher or lower category, or to Refuted, when
  the evidence changes. It stays visible under its new category.
- **Correction or duplicate.** A Curator deactivates the entity and can link it to its
  replacement.
  A deactivated entity disappears from public views but stays in the database.

Public pages and the API show the active review and the active status of active entities. The
**Last reviewed** date on an entity page is the date of the active review. The API field
`last_update` gives the most recent of the entry date, the active status date and the active
review date.

The systematic reassessment of existing entities by Reviewers is called **re-review**. It works
through the same records: a re-review produces a new review and status that a Curator approves
(see [Re-review instructions](06-re-review-instructions.qmd)).

## Identifiers and vocabularies

SysNDD links every record to standard identifiers. Write them with an uppercase prefix and no
space after the colon.

| What | Source | Format | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gene | [HGNC](https://www.genenames.org/) | `HGNC:` + number | `HGNC:20153` (*CHD8*) |
| Mode of inheritance | [HPO](https://hpo.jax.org/) | `HP:` + 7 digits | `HP:0000006` |
| Disease | [OMIM](https://www.omim.org/) | `OMIM:` + 6 digits | `OMIM:615032` |
| Disease without OMIM entry | [MONDO](https://mondo.monarchinitiative.org/) | `MONDO:` + 7 digits | `MONDO:0001071` (intellectual disability) |
| Phenotype | [HPO](https://hpo.jax.org/) | `HP:` + 7 digits | `HP:0000256` (Macrocephaly) |
| Variation | [VariO](https://variationontology.org/) | `VariO:` + 4 digits | `VariO:0015` (protein truncation) |
| Publication | [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) | `PMID:` + number | `PMID:31721432` |
| Entity | SysNDD | number | `856`, shown as **sysndd:856** |

Some disease identifiers carry a suffix, such as `OMIM:300100_1`. The suffix separates several
SysNDD disease records that share one OMIM number, for example because OMIM lists the disease
for more than one gene or inheritance. API responses give this value as
`disease_ontology_id_version`.

### Modes of inheritance

SysNDD uses the HPO inheritance terms, for example Autosomal dominant inheritance, Autosomal
recessive inheritance, X-linked recessive inheritance and Mitochondrial inheritance. Panels and
filters group them into four groups: Autosomal dominant, Autosomal recessive, X-linked and Other.

### Phenotypes

Phenotypes are HPO terms from a fixed list of phenotype categories used across SysNDD. Each
phenotype on an entity has a **modifier**:

| `modifier_id` | Modifier |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | present |
| 2 | uncertain |
| 3 | variable |
| 4 | rare |
| 5 | absent |

Variation terms allow only present (1) and absent (5). Guidance on which phenotypes to record
is in the [Re-review instructions](06-re-review-instructions.qmd).

The current list of phenotype categories is available from the API at
`/api/list/phenotype`.

### Variation

The Variation Ontology (VariO) describes the types and effects of variants, such as protein
truncation or nonsynonymous variation. A variation term is recorded as present or absent. The
terms available for curation are listed at `/api/list/variation_ontology`. Reviewer guidance on
choosing terms is in the [Re-review instructions](06-re-review-instructions.qmd).

Some variation terms are suggested from external sources such as ClinVar. The entity page marks
them **Not yet confirmed by a curator** until a Curator confirms them. In API responses these
terms carry a `provenance` field whose `state` is `active_unconfirmed` or `confirmed`; its
`sources` name the external source. A term whose `provenance` is null was entered by a curator.

## What SysNDD does not curate

The gene page also shows data from other resources, such as gnomAD constraint scores and ClinVar
variants. These data are fetched for display. They are not part of the curated entity and do not
affect its evidence category. The exception is a variation term suggested from ClinVar, which is
shown on the entity with its provenance (see [Variation](#variation)).

Derived analyses, such as phenotype clusters and functional clusters, are computed from the
curated data. They are hypotheses, not curated facts (see
[Explore the analyses](using-analyses.qmd)).

## Database schema for developers

The database runs on MySQL. The authoritative schema is the migration history in the
repository folder `db/migrations/`, applied at startup. The
[Development](08-development.qmd) chapter explains how to work with it.

## Common problems

- **A gene appears twice in the entity table.** That is expected: each row is an entity, and a
  gene can have several. Use **Tables › Panels** or `/api/panels/browse` for one row per gene.
- **An entity has disappeared.** It was probably deactivated as a duplicate or replaced after a
  disease correction. Search for the gene to find the current entity.
- **The category in an older paper differs from today's.** Categories change when new evidence
  is approved. Cite the access date when you report a category.
